history.summary: Famous Ram temple at Ramrajatala, Santragachi, Howrah (29 Ramrajatala Station Road, 711104) - the neighbourhood is named after it. Zamindar Ayodhya Ram Chaudhury started a public (barowari) Rama puja here around 1740, reportedly after a divine instruction. Local tradition: villagers first opposed it as Saraswati Puja dominated the area, so a Saraswati idol was placed atop the Ram-Sita idols, a custom that continues. Claimed to be the only temple in the country where Rama is worshipped as a king along with his kingdom. The Ram Puja runs from Ram Navami (Chaitra-Baisakh) to the last Sunday of Bengali Shravan month, making it one of the longest-running temple fairs in West Bengal. IDENTITY CONFIRMED - well-documented.

name: Ramrajatala Ram Temple
town_description: Ramrajatala is a neighbourhood in Howrah city, West Bengal, between Howrah and Santragachi. Named after its Ram temple, it is a densely settled, culturally active suburb within the Kolkata Metropolitan Development Authority area.

travel.airport: Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose International Airport, Kolkata (~20 km)
travel.railway: Ramrajatala station on the Howrah-Kharagpur line, ~7 minutes walk from the temple; Howrah station ~3 km
travel.road: 29 Ramrajatala Station Road, Santragachi, Howrah 711104; buses including route 52 from Esplanade/Howrah; autos from Howrah station.

visitor_information.best_time: Ram Navami (March-April) through Shravan for the four-month puja and fair; October-March generally.
